full_caption: Larkspur Hill Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellant, v. Copperfield Row Development Partners, L.P., Appellee
court: Sable Land and Property Court, Cobbleton Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Larkspur Hill Capital Servicing, LLC appeals the denial by the Cobbleton County Board of Adjustment of a use variance permitting operation of a veterinary clinic at 4299 Old Quarry Turnpike, Cobbleton, SB, a parcel zoned R-2 single-family residential.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Vested rights against a subsequent ordinance arise where the developer, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has made substantial expenditures. Larkspur Hill Capital Servicing, LLC expended $510,000 on site work before the moratorium was adopted.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Hardship must arise from the land itself and not from the owner's personal circumstances or from a self-created condition. Purchase with knowledge of the restriction is a factor but is not, standing alone, disqualifying.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Spot zoning is the singling out of a small parcel for treatment differing from that of surrounding property, for the benefit of the owner and to the detriment of the comprehensive plan. The rezoning here served a plan objective and is not spot zoning.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Discontinuance for 6 months is presumed abandonment under Section 3.9 of the ordinance. The presumption is rebutted by proof of an intent to resume coupled with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A use variance requires proof of unnecessary hardship: that the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any permitted use, that the hardship is unique to the parcel, and that the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The board's findings must be sufficient to permit meaningful review. Conclusory recitals tracking the language of the ordinance, without reference to record evidence, require remand.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The parcel is 380 square feet, irregular in shape, and burdened by a drainage easement across 3 percent of its buildable area. Those are conditions of the land and not of the owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: A nonconforming use lawfully existing at the effective date of the ordinance may continue but may not be enlarged, and is lost by abandonment or by discontinuance for the period specified in the ordinance.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: An area variance is governed by a balancing test weighing the benefit to the applicant against the detriment to the health, safety and welfare of the neighborhood, and does not require the showing of hardship applicable to use variances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is a prerequisite to judicial review. A facial constitutional challenge to the ordinance is excepted from that requirement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The denial is vacated and the matter remanded to the Board for findings addressing the drainage easement and the shape of the parcel.

sections.heading: RIDER A — VARIANCE APPLICATION AND FINDINGS REQUIRED
sections.text: An application for a use variance shall be granted only upon written findings, supported by substantial evidence in the record, that: (1) the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any use permitted in the district; (2) the hardship arises from conditions unique to the parcel and not generally applicable in the district; (3) the hardship was not self-created; and (4) the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality. Findings that merely recite the language of this Rider without reference to record evidence are insufficient.

sections.heading: RIDER C — NONCONFORMING USE AND ABANDONMENT
sections.text: A use lawfully existing on the effective date of this ordinance may continue in its then-existing scope but shall not be enlarged, extended to additional land, or changed to another nonconforming use. Discontinuance of the use for 6 consecutive months creates a rebuttable presumption of abandonment, which may be overcome by evidence of an intent to resume together with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: RIDER D — VESTED RIGHTS AND MORATORIUM
sections.text: A permittee who, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has incurred substantial expenditures or substantially changed position acquires a vested right to complete the development in accordance with the permit, notwithstanding any subsequently adopted ordinance or moratorium. Expenditures for architectural, engineering and permitting services alone are not 'substantial' for purposes of this Rider unless they exceed 3 percent of the total project cost.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Sable, the period is extended to the next business day.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 7 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $500,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.
